method: Read existing object assembly with otool -tvV; no source compilation or benchmark execution. Normalize function addresses and branch destinations relative to function start; strip adrp page comments.
findings: V1 numeric_value reserves 112 bytes and copies 72 bytes of descriptor on retained reads.
V2 numeric_value reserves 48 bytes because scalar decoders are fully inlined; its plain DTA path has no scalar cache access and no extra call.
Baseline numeric_value reserves 32 bytes and tail-transfers to typed decoders that each reserve48bytes. V2 removes that second prologue/epilogue sequence.
V2 has no local numeric_data descriptor and no 72-byte descriptor copy.
All four general numeric_TYPE_value_at instruction sequences are unchanged after address normalization.
Cache miss calls are confined to retained branches. Timing must confirm effect; assembly alone does not establish speedup.
call_site_note: Static call-site counts include error branches and retained cache misses. The ordinary DTA path has the same three R API calls before value decoding in both baseline and v2, and no additional decoder call in v2.
